newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-NEWCASTLE UNITED V MIDDLESBROUGH TACTICS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-NEWCASTLE UNITED V MIDDLESBROUGH TACTICS.

text.p: A look at the strengths and weaknesses of Newcastle United and Middlesbrough who meet in the English premier league at St James' Park on Sunday (kickoff 1600 gmt):

Playing style: An expansive style of exciting, attacking soccer has taken Newcastle to the top of the league but defensive frailties could still cost them real success. Manager Kevin Keegan's adventurous approach often means they keep on attacking when a game has been won with defenders still pushing up when other teams would stay back. Whatever formation Keegan starts with, whether it be 3-5-2, 4-4-2 or even 4-3-3, it often ends up looking more like 0-5-5 with every player looking to get forward and score.

Strengths: With 19 goals already between them this season, the real power is focused up front in England strikers Alan Shearer and Les Ferdinand. With Shearer currently sidelined, Ferdinand is still capable of leading the line alone and gets plenty of service from wide men David Ginola and Keith Gillespie. And when he's on-form, Colombian international Faustino Asprilla is a handy partner to have up front.

Weaknesses: The defence. Newcastle leave too many gaps at the back as a result of their aggressive, attacking play. While individually all the defenders are good players, they look vulnerable as a unit and erratic goalkeeping from Pavel Srnicek can do little to ease their collective state of mind.

Motivation: Having gone so close to the title last season and signed Shearer for a world record fee of 15 million pounds, ($24 million), nothing less than a major trophy will do this season. In descending order the goals are the league championship, the F.A. Cup, the UEFA Cup, the league cup. It's been 69 years since Newcastle last won the title, 41 years since they last won the F.A. Cup, 27 years since they won the old Inter Cities Fairs Cup, their last major honour. Their fans are tired of waiting.

Playing style: Coach Bryan Robson seems to have graduated from the Kevin Keegan school of soccer philosophy that attack -- and lots of it -- is the best form of defence. Most of the millions he has spent on the team have been on forwards and midfielders with the result that Middlesbrough --like Newcastle -- are exciting coming forward but leave gaps at the back.

Strengths: Skillful Brazilian midfielders Emerson and Juninho and the outstanding Fabrizio Ravanelli up front are the obvious stars in a side that can create goals out of nothing, especially on fast moving counter-attacks.

Weaknesses: Like Newcastle, Middlesbrough are vulnerable at the back where the lack of pace and cohesion has meant Middlesbrough have leaked 18 league goals this season, the worst in the premier league.

Motivation: Middlesbrough started the season brightly but have slipped to 13th after a run of disappointing results. There is nowhere better for them to start winning again that at the home of old rivals Newcastle.
